lemma: Suffix-separation lemma (deterministic, conditional on a collision). For every n≥1 and distinct u,v∈{0,1}^n, define y=u∧¬v if u∧¬v≠0, and otherwise y=v∧¬u. Then exactly one of u,v is disjoint from y. Consequently, for any deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm A whose states after u and v are equal, A gives the same answer on (u,y) and (v,y), although their DISJ answers differ, so A errs on at least one of these two inputs. Proof: In the first case, y has a 1 only where u has a 1 and v has a 0; hence u intersects y and v is disjoint from y. In the second case u∧¬v=0, so every 1 of u is also a 1 of v. Since u≠v, v∧¬u≠0; y is then disjoint from u and intersects v. Equal streaming states after the prefixes, followed by the same suffix, yield equal final states and outputs. This proves only suffix construction once a collision is supplied; it does not uniformly select a colliding pair or address randomized algorithms.

statement: For every n≥1 and distinct u,v∈{0,1}^n, let y=u∧¬v if u∧¬v≠0; otherwise let y=v∧¬u. Exactly one of u,v is disjoint from y. Thus, if a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm has the same state after u and v, it gives the same output on (u,y) and (v,y), although their DISJ answers differ, so it errs on at least one.
proof: If u∧¬v≠0, every 1-coordinate of y has u_i=1 and v_i=0; hence u intersects y and v is disjoint from y. Otherwise u_i≤v_i for every i. Since u≠v, some coordinate has v_i=1 and u_i=0, so y=v∧¬u is nonzero, u is disjoint from y, and v intersects y. In either case the two DISJ answers differ. Equal deterministic states after the prefixes, followed by the same suffix, produce the same final state and output.

statement: For every n≥1 and fixed omitted coordinate i(n)∈[n], let σ_n(x)=x with coordinate i(n) deleted. The prefixes u_n=0^n and v_n=e_{i(n)} collide under σ_n, and the common suffix y_n=e_{i(n)} gives DISJ(u_n,y_n)=1 and DISJ(v_n,y_n)=0. If i(n) is computable by a polylogtime-uniform AC0 family (in particular, if i(n)=1), these prefix and suffix families are uniformly AC0-constructible.
proof: Deleting coordinate i(n) makes u_n and v_n identical on every retained coordinate, so σ_n(u_n)=σ_n(v_n). The all-zero string is disjoint from y_n, while v_n=e_{i(n)} intersects y_n at coordinate i(n), giving opposite DISJ answers. The construction outputs zeros or the unit vector at i(n); under the stated uniformity assumption these strings are generated by the corresponding uniform AC0 family.

statement: Fix an integer q>=1 and a deterministic one-pass streaming machine A with at most q states. For each n>=q and j in {0,...,q}, let x_j(n)=1^j0^(n-j). Then there is a fixed pair 0<=a<b<=q such that A reaches the same state after x_a(n) and x_b(n) for infinitely many n. Each of the two prefix families is polylogtime-uniform AC0 constructible. For those infinitely many n, the suffix-separation lemma supplies a common suffix on which the two DISJ answers differ.
proof: For each n>=q, the q+1 prefixes x_0(n),...,x_q(n) lead to at most q states. Thus some pair (a_n,b_n) with a_n<b_n collides. There are only binom(q+1,2) possible pairs. If each pair collided at only finitely many n, the union of those finite sets of lengths would be finite, contradicting that a colliding pair exists for every n>=q. Hence one fixed pair (a,b) collides for infinitely many n. For fixed a, x_a(n) is generated by outputting a initial 1s followed by n-a zeros, which is a uniform AC0 family; likewise for b. At each collision length, apply the suffix-separation lemma to x_a(n),x_b(n). This proves the stated result. The pair depends on A, and this argument does not select it uniformly from A.
